newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian firm to pump 3,000 bpd condensate in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian firm to pump 3,000 bpd condensate in 1997.

text.p: A subsidiary of state-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) will produce 3,000 barrels per day (bpd) of condensate early in 1997 from its Oredo oilfield in the Midwestern area, an official spokesman said on Tuesday.

"About 3,000 bpd of condensate will be produced from the Nigeria Petroleum Development Company (NPDC) Oredo field under the second phase of its development," the NPDC spokesman told reporters in Lagos.
Under the first phase of its development, the Oredo field, which is located on oil mining lease 110, is currently producing 15,000 bpd of condensate.
Two wells will come into production under the second phase and will yield 50 billion cubic feet of gas daily, the NPDC spokesman said.
Most of Nigeria's gas output, produced during the pumping of crude oil, is currently flared.
The NPDC spokesman said: "The gas will be sold to the Nigeria Gas Company for domestic consumption while the condensate will be sold as crude oil."
Nigeria is Africa's largest oil producer, pumping about two million bpd.
